author: Paweł Krzywdziński
name: StateUI App
description: A .NET MAUI application whose user interface is written in Swift: one page, a counter, and the build that compiles the Swift side for every platform.
//sourceName: Every occurrence of StateUIStarter becomes the name given to -n, in file
names as well as in the files themselves. The token is deliberately not
properties, and they are the build's own, not this application's - renaming
them would leave a project that builds nothing and says nothing about why.

//applicationId: The bundle identifier is lower case on every platform, so the name has to
arrive here in that form as well - com.example.stateuistarter becomes
com.example.mynewapp. The Android manifest, both Info.plist files and the
.csproj all read it from $(ApplicationId), so this one replacement covers

modifiers.//: Build products, in case the template was ever built in place.

//: THE BUILD SCRIPTS ARE COPIED BYTE FOR BYTE, and this is not tidiness.
The templating engine EVALUATES MSBuild Condition attributes in the
files it writes: measured on StateUI.targets, `Condition="'@(x)' == ''"`
read as false and took the whole element with it, while
`Condition="'@(x)' != ''"` read as true and had the attribute stripped.
What went were the two <Error> guards that say a Swift build produced
no native library - so an app would have packaged silently without any
Swift in it, which is the one failure this project cannot see. The
.csproj beside them came through untouched, which is what made it look
like nothing had happened. Nothing under .scripts/ carries the name of
the application anyway, so there is nothing to replace there.
